title: The Hollow Harvest
text: Every ear of wheat in the city's fields has come up hollow, and inside each one is a pale seed, soft, warm, the size of a fingernail. The bakers will not touch it. The city needs grain bought in from the far valleys before the winter, and iron to burn the fields clean.

temptation.label: Grind the pale seeds into flour and sell it to the poor.
temptation.text: The bread is fine. Better than fine. The poor who eat it sleep well and dream of a mother none of them have met.

triumph.text: The fields are burned, the seeds with them, and the bought grain gets the city through. The smoke smells of milk for a week.

holds.text: Enough grain comes in. Nobody can say for certain every pale seed was burned.

falters.text: Not enough grain, and not enough fire. The hungry eat the seeds. They are very calm afterwards, and very hungry.

calamity.text: The pale seeds sprout in the granaries, in the gutters, in the mouths of the dead. Something in the far dark has found the city's soil to its liking.
